bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: CenterPoint Energy
providers.description: CenterPoint Energy is a domestic energy delivery company that provides electric transmission and distribution, natural gas distribution, and energy services operations serving residential, commercial, and industrial customers across multiple U.S. states. Developer-facing interfaces include the Smart Meter Texas (SMT) Usage History Inquiry API, Green Button Connect My Data exports for authorized third-party access to customer interval usage, and the Centerpoint Connect service API at api-portal.centerpointconnect.io used by contractor and field-service integrations.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: Sempra Energy
providers.description: Sempra Energy is a San Diego-headquartered North American energy infrastructure holding company and a Fortune 500 constituent, operating regulated utilities and energy infrastructure across California, Texas and Mexico. Its businesses include San Diego Gas & Electric and Southern California Gas Company in California, Oncor Electric Delivery in Texas, and Sempra Infrastructure, which develops LNG export terminals, natural gas pipelines and renewable generation in North America. Sempra operates a Google Apigee API program — an API gateway at api.sempra.com and a developer portal at developer.sempra.com inviting developers to "sign up today and start using Sempra APIs" — but publishes no API product, contract or reference to unauthenticated visitors, so the entire integration surface sits behind portal registration.

providers.name: AMSC
providers.description: American Superconductor Corporation (AMSC) is a power control systems company headquartered in Ayer, Massachusetts, and traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker AMSC. The company designs and delivers grid and power-electronics solutions across three specialties - power supply, power protection, and power innovation - serving the energy, renewables, utility, industrial, materials, and military sectors. Its offerings span grid capacity and resiliency systems, renewable generation integration, industrial process power control, and shipboard power protection for naval defense. AMSC is an early Battery Ventures portfolio investment. AMSC does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's corporate identity and domain security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Optiwatt
providers.description: Optiwatt is a consumer-centric energy management platform that helps electric-vehicle drivers and homeowners lower their electricity bills by automatically scheduling EV charging and smart-thermostat use for off-peak, low-cost, and low-carbon hours. Its consumer app (getoptiwatt.com) connects to vehicles, chargers, and thermostats via direct OEM integrations such as the Tesla Fleet API and aggregators like Smartcar, while its utility platform (optiwatt.com) orchestrates these distributed energy resources as virtual power plants across demand-response and load-shaping programs for utility partners. Backed by GV. Optiwatt is primarily a consumer of third-party APIs rather than a public API producer; no public developer API or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: David Energy
providers.description: David Energy is a clean-energy technology company and licensed electricity retailer that installs free plug-in smart batteries for homes and businesses. Its software charges batteries when grid power is cheap and discharges them during peak-price periods to lower customers' monthly utility bills, alongside bill-monitoring and thermostat-management advisory tools. Backed by Union Square Ventures, David Energy operates in the New York City market with a stated mission of powering the grid on 100% clean energy and shifting the balance of energy control from institutions toward consumers.

providers.name: AutoGrid
providers.description: AutoGrid Systems is a United States grid-technology company founded in 2011 by Amit Narayan in Redwood City, California, that built AI and machine-learning software for distributed energy resource management (DERMS), virtual power plants, and automated demand response under the AutoGrid Flex platform, selling to investor-owned utilities, retailers, and aggregators rather than to end consumers. It sits on the grid-tech / DERMS layer of the energy value chain - a buyer and orchestrator of utility and device data, not a data custodian - so no Green Button, Consumer Data Right, or smart-meter data-sharing obligation attaches to it. Schneider Electric took control of AutoGrid and then sold it to Uplight in a deal announced 14 December 2023 and closed in early 2024; auto-grid.com now serves only a 270-byte meta-refresh to uplight.com (on an expired TLS certificate as of 27 July 2026) and every developer, docs, api, and data subdomain fails to resolve. Its API posture is therefore honestly none-published - no public developer portal, no OpenAPI, no SDK, no consumer usage API, and no open market data. Its machine-readable contract is instead expressed as protocol conformance, and that is real and still published by the certifying bodies. AutoGrid is a certified OpenADR 2.0a and 2.0b VTN (server) - AutoGrid DROMS and OpenDR Server 2.0, Simple HTTP + XMPP, pull and push - and holds SunSpec Alliance certificate CS-000074 for AutoGrid Flex as an IEEE 2030.5-2018 / CSIP server, tested by Intertek on 12 December 2023 and awarded 22 January 2024. Both surfaces authenticate with mutual TLS x.509 client certificates and were reachable only under commercial contract. The successor surface at docs.uplight.com is real but fully login-gated, redirecting anonymous visitors to a ReadMe dashboard login, and api.uplight.com answers HTTP 401 with "Invalid or no token provided" - partner and customer access only.

providers.name: AGL Resources
providers.description: AGL Resources was an energy services holding company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, whose principal business was the distribution of natural gas to residential, commercial, and industrial customers. In 2016, AGL Resources was acquired by Southern Company and renamed Southern Company Gas, becoming the nation's largest natural gas-only distribution company. The company distributes natural gas through subsidiaries including Atlanta Gas Light, Chattanooga Gas, Nicor Gas, and Virginia Natural Gas. AGL Resources / Southern Company Gas does not offer a public developer API; utility data access is available through third-party data aggregators and community-built integrations.

providers.name: rabot.energy
providers.description: rabot.energy (RABOT Energy DE GmbH) is a Hamburg-based German electricity supplier offering dynamic and fixed-rate power tariffs where consumers pay hourly rates that track the wholesale electricity market. The company provides 100% renewable energy certified by TÜV NORD, smart meter installation and management, EV charging optimization (Autostrom), and home battery storage (Rabot Flow), all managed through a consumer mobile app for consumption monitoring. It is a consumer-facing energy retailer; no public developer portal or API is currently published. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital.

providers.name: Portland General Electric
providers.description: Portland General Electric is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Portland General Electric API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: South Jersey Industries
providers.description: South Jersey Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The South Jersey Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: SpryPoint
providers.description: SpryPoint is a cloud-based customer service and operations software provider for utilities, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, Canada. Its platform modernizes the meter-to-cash lifecycle for water & sewer, electric, and gas utilities across North America through an integrated suite of modules: SpryCIS (customer information system), SpryEngage (omnichannel customer portal), SpryWallet (payment processing), SpryMobile MFS (field service orders), SpryMobile WOAM (work order and asset management), SpryBackflow (backflow compliance), and SpryIDM (interval data management). The company serves 100+ utility clients, employs 285+ people, is SOC 2 audited, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Insight Partners. SpryPoint publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; integrations are delivered through partnership engagements rather than a self-service API.

providers.name: Project Canary
providers.description: Project Canary is a Denver-based climate technology company that helps oil and gas operators and natural gas utilities turn methane emissions data into operational intelligence. Founded in 2019, its Canary SENSE platform unifies measurement data from sensors, satellites, aircraft, SCADA, and field teams into a single view that drives decisions, reduces costs, and supports regulatory reporting (OGMP 2.0 and other frameworks). The company builds high-precision methane detection hardware (Canary RECON, Aeris PICO) and a proprietary predictive emissions model (methaneML) trained on a multi-year, high-fidelity methane dataset, serving upstream and midstream operators as well as gas distribution utilities across the United States. Project Canary has raised $121M (Series B) and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and Techstars. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI is published at this time; this profile captures identity, a verbatim llms.txt, and security posture.

providers.name: Sealed
providers.description: Sealed is a New York-based climate technology company, founded in 2012, whose Sealed Pro platform helps home-improvement contractors sell and finance home weatherization and electrification projects — insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, smart thermostats and heat-pump water heaters. Sealed pairs energy data and analytics with a rebate and incentive engine that qualifies a project at the point of sale, guarantees a minimum rebate amount, files the utility and Inflation Reduction Act (HOMES / HEAR) paperwork on the contractor's behalf, and pays the contractor after installation while Sealed carries the incentive-collection risk. The company began as a direct-to-consumer home energy retrofit provider with the first residential energy-savings guarantee, and relaunched as Sealed Pro, a contractor-facing software platform, working with utilities and state energy offices on measured- and modeled-savings programs.

providers.name: Dycom Industries
providers.description: Dycom Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Dycom Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Powerledger
providers.description: Powerledger (Powerledger AG / Power Ledger Pty Ltd, Perth, Western Australia) builds software for tracking, tracing and trading renewable energy and environmental commodities. Its platform is modular and sold to utilities, retailers, network operators, generators and corporates rather than to developers: xGrid and uGrid for peer-to-peer energy trading across and behind the meter, TraceX as a marketplace for Renewable Energy Certificates and other Energy Attribute Certificates (integrated with the M-RETS and ERCOT registries), Vision and PPA Vision for 24/7 renewable portfolio and PPA tracking, plus hydrogen and EV settlement products. Powerledger originally ran its own permissioned Solana-derived chain (the Powerledger Energy Blockchain, source at github.com/PowerLedger/powr) and has since moved to Solana mainnet, where the POWR SPL token lives. As of this profile Powerledger publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Beacon Power Services
providers.description: Beacon Power Services (BPS) is an African energy-technology company building software that helps electricity utilities and energy consumers manage the power grid more efficiently. Its platform spans three products: CAIMS, a customer and asset information management system for utility network, survey, installation, and new-service-connection management; Adora, a grid network management solution for commercial operations, network management, and field operations that helps utilities optimize operations and increase profitability; and Xepp, a consumer mobile app for energy consumption monitoring, instant electricity top-up, solar integration, and flexible payments. BPS serves utilities and distribution companies across Africa (clients include ECG and AEDC) and is backed by Partech. This profile currently has no public API or developer surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Excelergy
providers.description: Excelergy is a global provider of high-performance retail energy billing and revenue management software, now part of Harris Computer. Its flagship product, RevenueManager, is a cloud-based, meter-to-cash billing platform used by competitive energy retailers across more than 200 jurisdictions in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. RevenueManager handles residential, commercial, industrial, and wholesale billing across multiple commodities (electricity, natural gas, water, heat, and sewage), supporting complex tariff and pricing models, customer lifecycle management, smart-meter and time-of-use pricing, and built-in Salesforce CRM integration. The platform exposes APIs for connectivity with third-party systems and access to data held in the RevenueManager database. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; Excelergy publishes a corporate marketing site and a customer support portal but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Tantalus
providers.description: Tantalus Systems (TSX: GRID; OTCQX: TGMPF) is a technology company that has served public power utilities and electric cooperatives for over 35 years, modernizing electrical distribution grids through data-centric solutions. Its Tantalus Grid Modernization Platform (TGMP) unifies intelligence across the distribution grid, connecting metering, load and DER management, grid automation, and data management across both legacy and modern infrastructure. Product lines include TRUConnect advanced metering infrastructure (AMI), TRUFlex load and DER management, TRUGrid automation analytics, TRUSync grid data management, and the TRUSense behind-the-meter gateway. Tantalus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; integration with back-end utility software is delivered through standard data formats and handled via its technical support and integration teams.

providers.name: The Human Utility
providers.description: The Human Utility (formerly the Detroit Water Project) is a Y Combinator-backed not-for-profit organization founded in 2014 by Tiffani Ashley Bell whose mission is to preserve human dignity by increasing water affordability for families across the United States. It matches families who are behind on their water bills with donors who want to help, paying utility companies directly on their behalf through crowdfunded donations, community-building, and policy action. Operating in Detroit, Baltimore, and dozens of other cities, it has helped thousands of households avoid water shutoffs. The Human Utility runs a public-facing web application for donors and recipients rather than a developer-facing API product; its source code lives in the humanutility GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with identity and link details; no public API surface was found.

providers.name: Westar Energy
providers.description: Westar Energy was the largest electric utility in Kansas, providing electric service to homes, businesses, and industries throughout Kansas before merging with Great Plains Energy in 2018 to form Evergy, Inc. As Evergy, the company continues to serve approximately 1.6 million customers in Kansas and Missouri with a focus on grid modernization, smart metering (AMI) through its Gridstream Connect IoT platform, and clean energy transformation including wind power and demand response programs.

providers.name: Dynegy
providers.description: Dynegy is a retail electric service provider and part of the Vistra Corp family of companies, delivering simple, price-protected retail electricity plans for homes and businesses across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Midwest, including Ohio, Illinois, and Pennsylvania. No public APIs have been documented for Dynegy.

providers.name: Globetouch
providers.description: Globetouch is a global mobile and IoT connectivity provider founded in 2010 and headquartered in San Ramon, California, which rebranded to Airlinq in February 2020 — globetouch.com now 301-redirects to www.airlinq.com. Its GConnect / CloudSIM heritage (physical SIM, soft SIM and eSIM provisioning with rule-engine-driven subscription-profile management for mobile operators and IoT enterprises) is carried forward in Mobilinq, the company's IoT connectivity and application management platform, alongside Autolinq for the connected-vehicle ecosystem, Utilinq for electric, gas and water utilities, and Marketlinq, an operator-branded private-5G and IoT marketplace and dashboard. Airlinq markets a "comprehensive API library" for BSS/OSS integration and data and voice plans "enabled via API", but as of August 2026 it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind; the only entry point is a contact-sales form.

providers.name: Exelon
providers.description: Exelon Corporation is one of the largest energy delivery companies in the United States, serving more than 10 million customers through its regulated electric and gas utility subsidiaries: Atlantic City Electric, BGE, ComEd, Delmarva Power, PECO, and Pepco. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, Exelon operates across multiple U.S. states. No public consumer-facing developer APIs have been identified for Exelon; customer self-service is conducted through utility portals.

providers.name: American Electric Power
providers.description: American Electric Power (AEP) is one of the largest electric utilities in the United States, delivering electricity to more than 5.6 million customers across 11 states through its regulated utility subsidiaries including AEP Ohio, AEP Texas, Appalachian Power, Indiana Michigan Power, Kentucky Power, Public Service Company of Oklahoma, and Southwestern Electric Power Company. AEP operates the nation's largest electricity transmission network spanning over 40,000 miles and maintains approximately 31,000 megawatts of generating capacity.

providers.name: Riggs Distler
providers.description: Riggs Distler & Company is an energy and utility infrastructure construction firm operating since 1909. Now part of Centuri Group, the company delivers electric transmission and distribution, natural gas, renewable energy, emergency response, and heavy civil services across the United States and Canada. Riggs Distler is a field-services contractor with no public developer APIs or developer portal.

providers.name: Eneryield
providers.description: Eneryield is a Gothenburg, Sweden based company (a Techstars portfolio company) building AI-powered fault prediction and analytics for electric power systems. Its flagship product, Eneryield IntelliView, uses explainable AI to forecast power outages before they occur by analyzing voltage and current signals from digital relays and merging units on overhead lines, underground cables, and underwater cables. The cloud-based platform integrates directly into existing utility monitoring systems without additional hardware, giving grid operators transparent root-cause analysis so they can move to proactive maintenance and reduce operational cost and downtime. As of this profile, Eneryield publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this record captures its identity and infrastructure posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PSEG
providers.description: Public Service Enterprise Group (PSEG) is a diversified energy holding company headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. Its regulated utility subsidiary Public Service Electric and Gas (PSE&G) is New Jersey's largest electric and gas distribution utility, and PSEG Long Island operates the transmission and distribution system on behalf of the Long Island Power Authority. PSEG sits squarely in the utility-retailer tier of the United States energy value chain — it meters, bills, and serves end customers, and it sells generation into the PJM wholesale market rather than publishing that market's data itself. Its API posture is honestly closed. There is no developer portal: developer., developers., api., docs., and data.pseg.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, and /docs on pseg.com return the site's soft-404 page. Green Button is present only as a file: PSEG Long Island's MySmartEnergy FAQ states customers can "download data information in CSV or Green Button (.XML) format," which is Download My Data behind a customer login, not Connect My Data. There is no documented programmatic third-party access to customer usage data — in the New Jersey BPU AMI docket PSE&G described manual secondary-user sharing, a Letter of Authorization with spreadsheets emailed back, and EDI for BPU-licensed suppliers. Grid data is equally closed: the PSE&G NJ and PSEG Long Island outage maps are vendor-hosted KUBRA StormCenter applications with no published data API. Open market data for this territory comes from PJM and the EIA, not from PSEG.

providers.name: Sense
providers.description: Sense is a Cambridge, Massachusetts energy-intelligence company that builds a residential energy monitor and machine-learning platform for real-time whole-home electricity disaggregation. The Sense Monitor installs in a home electrical panel, samples voltage and current at one million times per second, and uses signature-based machine-learning models to identify individual appliances and loads behind a single point of measurement. The Sense iOS, Android, and web apps surface device-level usage, always-on load, solar production, time-of-use cost, and goal tracking to homeowners. For utilities and grid operators, Sense embeds its disaggregation software into next-generation AMI 2.0 smart meters through partnerships with meter manufacturers such as Landis+Gyr, providing grid-edge visibility, fault detection, load-management, demand-response, and virtual-power-plant enablement. Sense also runs a partner program for smart-device integration with thermostats, EV chargers, heat pumps, and home-service providers. Sense has not released an official public developer API; community developers maintain reverse-engineered, unofficial clients in Python, Node.js, and Home Assistant against an undocumented and unsupported endpoint. Sense's revenue model is hardware sales of the consumer monitor and licensing of its disaggregation software to utilities and meter OEMs.

providers.name: Bidgely
providers.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

providers.name: Valor Water Analytics
providers.description: Valor Water Analytics was a San Francisco-based water analytics company that built financial data and dashboard tools for water utilities, including leak and revenue-loss detection. A Y Combinator, Imagine H2O, and 500 Global portfolio company, it was acquired by Xylem Inc. (completed February 2, 2018) and folded into Xylem's digital portfolio, now represented by the Xylem Vue platform. valorwater.com redirects to Xylem Vue, and no independent API surface remains published.

providers.name: Calpine
providers.description: Calpine Corporation was a major U.S. energy company headquartered in Houston, Texas, and was the largest generator of electricity from natural gas and geothermal energy in the United States. It operated 80 power plants with approximately 26,035 megawatts of generation capacity, including The Geysers, the world's largest geothermal complex. Calpine also operated the Champion Energy retail electricity subsidiary serving deregulated markets. As of January 2026, Constellation Energy completed its acquisition of Calpine for $16.4 billion, making it a business unit of Constellation. Calpine does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: MDU Resources Group
providers.description: MDU Resources Group is a diversified natural resources company with operations in regulated energy delivery, construction materials, and construction services. No public developer APIs are currently documented.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Azuria
providers.description: The website wired to this profile (azuria.com) resolves to Azuria Water Solutions, an infrastructure-rehabilitation company that has operated for over 50 years in the water, wastewater, and stormwater sector. It renews aging pipeline infrastructure through cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) technology, water main renewal, cathodic protection, and spray-on lining, operating through brands including Insituform, Underground Solutions, MTC, and Corrpro. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface: it is not an API provider. It provides energy, water, and waste expense management, utility bill auditing and payment, data management, sustainability consulting, and decarbonization strategy across a large portfolio of client sites. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile has been enriched with domain-security and discovery probes; the company publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

NextEra Energy operates principally through its two subsidiaries, Florida Power & Light (FPL) and NextEra Energy Resources. PSEG is a Fortune 500 company. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

In February 2017, Spectra Energy was acquired by Enbridge Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $28 billion and no longer operates as an independent entity.

providers.name: CES International
providers.description: CES International was a software company founded in 1989 and based in Alpharetta, Georgia, that built real-time software solutions for distribution utilities — including the Centricity operations resource management (ORM) system with outage-management capabilities and an energy delivery management (EDM) suite for network operations — serving utilities on five continents and more than 35 million metered accounts. It was acquired by SPL WorldGroup in May 2004, and SPL WorldGroup was in turn acquired by Oracle in November 2006, where its utilities software became the foundation of the Oracle Utilities global business unit. CES International no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface, and none of its historical domains resolve to a live company site. This record is retained as a historical / defunct entry in the API Evangelist network.

The company was acquired by Uplight, and the firstfuel.com domain now redirects to uplight.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The enrichment pipeline found no active first-party developer surface (no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve, and no OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP artifacts are published), so this profile remains an identity-only record for a company that no longer operates a standalone API program.

providers.name: Energy and Utilities
providers.description: Energy and Utilities is a topic profile in the API Evangelist Network cataloging the API surfaces that move data across the modern electricity, gas, and water value chain. It indexes utility data integration APIs, grid and wholesale market operator APIs, federal energy data programs, renewable energy research APIs, weather APIs that drive grid demand and solar forecasting, EV charging interoperability protocols, and the Green Button family of customer energy data standards. The repo provides a baseline catalog plus shared semantics (JSON Schema, JSON-LD, vocabulary, examples) for the meter reading / energy data point that ties every one of these surfaces together.
